title: Introduction to codeminer
text: multiple versions lookup, mapping, relationship table available, codeminer resolves "latest" automatically. first time query function resolves "latest" given code type, resolved version cached remainder session. avoids repeated informational messages ensures consistent version usage across workflow. can override current session codeminer_set_version(): Pins affect default "latest" resolution. Explicit version arguments always take precedence: clear version selections return automatic "latest" resolution: can also clear versions selectively code type: codeminer_status() shows active versions alongside connection info.
code: # Pin lookup and relationship versions for a code type codeminer_set_version(   lookup       = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4"),   relationship = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4") )  # Pin a mapping version (use "from > to" format for the key) codeminer_set_version(   mapping = c("Read 3 > ICD-10" = "UKB v4") ) # This uses the pinned version for ICD-10: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10  # This ignores the pin and uses "UKB v4" directly: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10", lookup_version = "UKB v4") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10 codeminer_clear_versions() # Clear only the ICD-10 lookup version codeminer_clear_versions(lookup = "ICD-10")  # Clear lookup and relationship for SNOMED CT codeminer_clear_versions(   lookup = "SNOMED CT",   relationship = "SNOMED CT" )

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: query functions accept col_filters parameter three options: "default" (default): apply filters session pin metadata defaults NULL: filtering — return rows regardless column values named list: apply explicit filters call
code: # Default: only active concepts (from metadata defaults) CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT")  # Override: return all rows including inactive CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT", col_filters = NULL)  # Custom: only inactive concepts CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT", col_filters = list(active_concept = c("0")))

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: important design point: table type independent col_filters. matters MAP(), touches two table types: mapping table (e.g., Read 3 → ICD-10) may filters like mapping_status target lookup table (e.g., ICD-10) may filters like active_concept call MAP(col_filters = ...), controls mapping table. target lookup table uses default filters looking descriptions. intentional — two tables different filterable columns different semantics. override filters target lookup well, use session pinning:
code: # Pin lookup filters for SNOMED CT codeminer_set_col_filters(   lookup = list("SNOMED CT" = list(active_concept = c("0", "1"))) )  # Now MAP() will use the pinned lookup filters for the target table MAP("24700007", from = "SNOMED CT", to = "ICD-10")

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: Like version pinning, can pin col_filters entire session:
code: # Pin: include inactive SNOMED concepts codeminer_set_col_filters(   lookup = list("SNOMED CT" = list(active_concept = c("0", "1"))) )  # Clear all filter pins codeminer_clear_col_filters()

title: Developer Guide
text: SNOMED CT GPS Release: dummy dataset uses concept codes SNOMED International GPS Release (available https://www.snomed.org/gps). GPS subset freely available can used testing purposes. Made-Data Convention: clearly distinguish fabricated test data authentic SNOMED CT content: Concept codes: Use pattern 000xxx000 (starting ending three zeros), e.g., 000001000, 000002000, 000100000 Description IDs: Use numeric IDs starting 000, e.g., 000010001, 000020001 Relationship IDs: Use numeric IDs starting 000, e.g., 000100001, 000100002 UUIDs (map refsets): Use pattern 00000xxx-0000-0000-0000-0000000000xx (starts five zeros, middle groups zeros), e.g., 10000001-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 Descriptions: Mark made-concept descriptions tildes ~description~, e.g., ~Optic neuritis due multiple sclerosis~ Examples: - 000001000 - Made-concept code - ~Optic neuritis due multiple sclerosis~ - Made-description - 10000001-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 - Made-UUID map refset entries
